description: Claude Code usage time per user, repository and workday from OTel prompt events: total and net prompt time, overlapping prompts, and when each workday started and ended.

links.title: Claude Prompts
links.tooltip: Back to the Claude Prompts dashboard, which uses UTC where this one uses your browser's timezone, so a relative range such as Today covers the UTC day there

panels.description: How long Claude Code was working for each user, per repository and workday. A workday is a run of the user's prompts, in any repository, with no break of ${workday_gap_hours} hours or more, and Date is the day it began. Workdays are found among the prompts you can see under the Project and Claude Code OTel teams filters, so changing those filters, or viewing with access to other projects, can split or join a workday; the User and Repository filters don't move workdays. Only workdays that began in the time range are shown, with all their prompts, even ones after the range ends. Claude Usage Time adds up every prompt's duration (started_at to ended_at); Net Claude Usage Time counts time when prompts in the same row overlapped once, and Overlapping Prompts counts the prompts that ran alongside another one in the row. Prompts in different repositories never count as overlapping, so the footer's net total can be more than a user's active time across repositories. Times are shown in your browser's timezone, while the other Claude dashboards use UTC, so a Date here can be a day off from their per-day charts. Repositories show as GH:, GL: or BB: (GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket, cloud or self-hosted) followed by their path, as on the Claude Prompts dashboards; other hosts show their host name. Details opens the row's prompts in Claude Prompt Details. Repository 'Unknown' means the session had no origin remote; Projects is every DevLake project you can access that collects the repository, 'Unmapped' when none does.

properties.value: Date the user's workday began, in your browser's timezone. A workday is a run of prompts with no long break (see the panel description), so it can cross midnight.
When the row's first prompt started, in your browser's timezone, with its offset from UTC. The Date column has the day.
When the row's last prompt finished, in your browser's timezone, with its offset from UTC. A workday can cross midnight, so this can be on the day after Date.
Sum of the row's prompt durations. Prompts that ran at the same time are each counted in full.
Prompts that ran while another prompt in this row was running.
Time when at least one prompt was running; overlapping prompts count once.
Opens this row's prompts in Claude Prompt Details, from the first prompt's start to just after the last one's end.

targets.rawSql:
-- base is every prompt the panel may count. run_ends, gaps and workdays split each user's prompts
-- into workdays, ordered and prev_ends find where each row's earlier prompts ended, islands groups
-- each user, repository and workday's prompts into stretches of continuous activity, i has one
-- row per island, and d one row per user, repository and workday.
WITH base AS (
  SELECT p.id,
    COALESCE(NULLIF(p.user_email, ''), p.user_key) AS user,
    NULLIF(TRIM(a.full_name), '') AS full_name,
    p.repository_url,
    p.started_at,
    p.ended_at
  FROM ai_prompts p
  -- account_id is the user's DevLake account, whose full_name the plugin copies from
  -- another account with the same email.
  LEFT JOIN accounts a ON a.id = p.account_id
  -- workday_gap_hours + 24 hours either side of the range too. Before it, so a workday that began
  -- earlier isn't taken to start at its first prompt inside the range: any prompt that ended within
  -- the gap before it started at most that long before, if no prompt runs over 24 hours. After it,
  -- so one that began in the range keeps its prompts after the range ends.
  WHERE p.started_at >= DATE_SUB($__timeFrom(), INTERVAL CAST(${workday_gap_hours} AS UNSIGNED) + 24 HOUR)
    AND p.started_at < DATE_ADD($__timeTo(), INTERVAL CAST(${workday_gap_hours} AS UNSIGNED) + 24 HOUR)
    -- The Project and team filters and the viewer's access apply before workdays are found, so
    -- they can move workday boundaries. Using prompts the viewer can't see would reveal their timing.
    -- '__all__' is every filter's allValue: All sends it instead of the option list, so an empty list
    -- can't produce IN (), and the access joins still limit what All covers.
    AND p.source_connection_id IN (SELECT c_g.id FROM _tool_claude_code_otel_connections c_g JOIN _tool_claude_code_otel_connection_projects cp_g ON cp_g.connection_id = c_g.id JOIN user_project_mapping upm_g ON upm_g.project_name = cp_g.project_name WHERE c_g.status = 'active' AND ('__all__' IN (${otel_teams:sqlstring}) OR c_g.team_slug IN (${otel_teams:sqlstring})) AND ('__all__' IN (${project:sqlstring}) OR cp_g.project_name IN (${project:sqlstring})) AND upm_g.user_login = ${__user.login:sqlstring})
    AND ('__all__' IN (${user:sqlstring}) OR COALESCE(NULLIF(p.user_email, ''), p.user_key) IN (${user:sqlstring}))
), run_ends AS (
  -- user_run_end is the latest end among the user's prompts so far, in any repository. A running
  -- max is computed incrementally; a frame that stops one row early is rescanned for every row.
  SELECT base.*,
    MAX(ended_at) OVER (PARTITION BY user ORDER BY started_at, id ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS user_run_end
  FROM base
), gaps AS (
  -- user_prev_end is the latest end among the user's earlier prompts, in any repository.
  SELECT run_ends.*,
    LAG(user_run_end) OVER (PARTITION BY user ORDER BY started_at, id) AS user_prev_end
  FROM run_ends
), workdays AS (
  -- A prompt that starts workday_gap_hours or more after the user's earlier prompts ended
  -- begins a new workday.
  SELECT gaps.*,
    SUM(CASE WHEN user_prev_end IS NULL OR started_at >= DATE_ADD(user_prev_end, INTERVAL CAST(${workday_gap_hours} AS UNSIGNED) HOUR) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
      OVER (PARTITION BY user ORDER BY started_at, id) AS workday
  FROM gaps
), w AS (
  SELECT workdays.*, MIN(started_at) OVER (PARTITION BY user, workday) AS workday_start
  FROM workdays
), ordered AS (
  -- row_run_end is the latest end among the row's prompts so far, as user_run_end above. Prompts
  -- that started at the same instant go shortest first, then by id, so a zero-duration prompt
  -- never joins the island of a longer one that started with it, whatever their ids.
  SELECT w.*,
    MAX(ended_at) OVER (PARTITION BY user, repository_url, workday ORDER BY started_at, ended_at, id
      ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS row_run_end
  FROM w
  -- Only workdays that began in the range, with all their prompts. The Repository filter applies
  -- here, after workdays are found, so it doesn't move their boundaries.
  WHERE w.workday_start >= $__timeFrom() AND w.workday_start < $__timeTo()
    AND ('__all__' IN (${repository:sqlstring}) OR COALESCE(w.repository_url, 'Unknown') IN (${repository:sqlstring}))
), prev_ends AS (
  -- prev_max_end is the latest end among the prompts that started before this one in its row.
  SELECT ordered.*,
    LAG(row_run_end) OVER (PARTITION BY user, repository_url, workday ORDER BY started_at, ended_at, id) AS prev_max_end
  FROM ordered
), islands AS (
  -- A prompt that starts at or after every earlier prompt has ended begins a new island. A
  -- prompt that starts while an earlier one is still running joins that island.
  SELECT prev_ends.*,
    SUM(CASE WHEN prev_max_end IS NULL OR started_at >= prev_max_end THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
      OVER (PARTITION BY user, repository_url, workday ORDER BY started_at, ended_at, id) AS island
  FROM prev_ends
), i AS (
  SELECT user, repository_url, workday, island,
    MAX(full_name) AS full_name,
    MIN(workday_start) AS workday_start,
    COUNT(*) AS prompts,
    MIN(started_at) AS island_start,
    MAX(ended_at) AS island_end,
    SUM(TIMESTAMPDIFF(MICROSECOND, started_at, ended_at)) / 1000000 AS secs
  FROM islands
  GROUP BY user, repository_url, workday, island
), d AS (
  SELECT user, repository_url, workday,
    MAX(full_name) AS full_name,
    MIN(workday_start) AS workday_start,
    MIN(island_start) AS first_start,
    MAX(island_end) AS last_end,
    SUM(secs) AS secs,
    -- Every prompt in an island of two or more overlaps at least one other prompt.
    SUM(CASE WHEN prompts > 1 THEN prompts ELSE 0 END) AS overlapping,
    SUM(TIMESTAMPDIFF(MICROSECOND, island_start, island_end)) / 1000000 AS net_secs
  FROM i
  GROUP BY user, repository_url, workday
)
-- The hint lifts GROUP_CONCAT's 1024-character default for this query, so a repository in many
-- projects isn't cut off in Projects.
SELECT /*+ SET_VAR(group_concat_max_len = 1048576) */ COALESCE(d.full_name, d.user) AS "User",
  -- Labelled as on the Claude Prompts dashboards: GH:, GL: or BB: and the path, or the host for other servers.
  CASE
    WHEN d.repository_url IS NULL THEN 'Unknown'
    WHEN d.repository_url REGEXP '^https?://([^/]*[.])?github[^/.]*[.][^/]+/' THEN REGEXP_REPLACE(d.repository_url, '^https?://[^/]+/', 'GH: ')
    WHEN d.repository_url REGEXP '^https?://([^/]*[.])?gitlab[^/.]*[.][^/]+/' THEN REGEXP_REPLACE(d.repository_url, '^https?://[^/]+/', 'GL: ')
    WHEN d.repository_url REGEXP '^https?://(www[.])?bitbucket[.]org/' THEN REGEXP_REPLACE(d.repository_url, '^https?://[^/]+/', 'BB: ')
    -- Bitbucket Server clone URLs carry an scm/ prefix that the SSH remote of the same repository lacks.
    WHEN d.repository_url REGEXP '^https?://([^/]*[.])?bitbucket[^/.]*[.][^/]+/' THEN REGEXP_REPLACE(d.repository_url, '^https?://[^/]+/(scm/)?', 'BB: ')
    ELSE REGEXP_REPLACE(d.repository_url, '^https?://', '')
  END AS "Repository",
  CASE WHEN d.repository_url IS NULL THEN 'No repository' ELSE COALESCE(dl.projects, 'Unmapped') END AS "Projects",
  -- A timestamp, not DATE(...): the panel formats it as a date in the browser's timezone.
  d.workday_start AS "Date",
  d.first_start AS "First Prompt Started",
  d.last_end AS "Last Prompt Completed",
  d.secs AS "Claude Usage Time",
  d.overlapping AS "Overlapping Prompts",
  d.net_secs AS "Net Claude Usage Time",
  -- Details holds the row's time span and filters as URL query parameters for its link to Prompt
  -- Details, and is displayed as "Details". Prompt Details filters on whole seconds, so the span
  -- runs to the second after the last prompt ended. The session is UTC, so UNIX_TIMESTAMP reads
  -- the UTC timestamps as they are. MySQL has no URL encoder, so the characters that would break
  -- a query string are escaped by hand, as on Claude Prompts.
  CONCAT('from=', FLOOR(UNIX_TIMESTAMP(d.first_start)) * 1000, '&to=', (FLOOR(UNIX_TIMESTAMP(d.last_end)) + 1) * 1000,
    '&var-user=', REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(d.user, '%', '%25'), '+', '%2B'), '&', '%26'), '#', '%23'), ' ', '%20'),
    '&var-repository=', REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(COALESCE(d.repository_url, 'Unknown'), '%', '%25'), '+', '%2B'), '&', '%26'), '#', '%23'), ' ', '%20')) AS "Details",
  -- repository_link is empty for prompts without a repository, so their Repository cell has no link.
  COALESCE(d.repository_url, '') AS repository_link
FROM d
LEFT JOIN (
  -- repository_url drops one trailing / and then one .git suffix, and is lowercased, so normalize
  -- repos.url the same way.
  SELECT LOWER(REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(rp.url, '/$', ''), '[.]git$', '')) AS url,
    GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT pm.project_name ORDER BY pm.project_name SEPARATOR ', ') AS projects
  FROM repos rp
  -- Only projects the viewer can access, so a repository shared with another project doesn't
  -- reveal its name.
  JOIN project_mapping pm ON pm.row_id = rp.id AND pm.`table` = 'repos'
    AND pm.project_name IN (SELECT upm_p.project_name FROM user_project_mapping upm_p WHERE upm_p.user_login = ${__user.login:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY LOWER(REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(rp.url, '/$', ''), '[.]git$', ''))
) dl ON dl.url = d.repository_url
ORDER BY d.workday_start DESC, d.secs DESC

list.definition:
SELECT DISTINCT p.name AS __text, p.name AS __value
FROM projects p
INNER JOIN _tool_claude_code_otel_connection_projects cp ON cp.project_name = p.name
INNER JOIN _tool_claude_code_otel_connections c ON c.id = cp.connection_id
INNER JOIN user_project_mapping upm ON upm.project_name = p.name
WHERE c.status = 'active'
  AND upm.user_login = ${__user.login:sqlstring}
ORDER BY p.name;

list.definition:
SELECT DISTINCT
    c.team_slug AS __text,
    c.team_slug AS __value
FROM _tool_claude_code_otel_connections AS c
INNER JOIN _tool_claude_code_otel_connection_projects AS cp
    ON cp.connection_id = c.id
WHERE c.status = 'active'
  AND (('__all__' IN (${project:sqlstring}) OR cp.project_name IN (${project:sqlstring})) AND cp.project_name IN (SELECT upm_g.project_name FROM user_project_mapping upm_g WHERE upm_g.user_login = ${__user.login:sqlstring}))
ORDER BY c.team_slug;

list.definition:
-- The label is the person's full name from their DevLake account, falling back to the email; the value stays the
-- email (or user key) that every panel filters on.
SELECT COALESCE(u.full_name, u.user) AS __text, u.user AS __value
FROM (
  SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(p.user_email, ''), p.user_key) AS user,
    MAX(NULLIF(TRIM(a.full_name), '')) AS full_name
  FROM ai_prompts p
  LEFT JOIN accounts a ON a.id = p.account_id
  WHERE p.source_connection_id IN (SELECT c_g.id FROM _tool_claude_code_otel_connections c_g JOIN _tool_claude_code_otel_connection_projects cp_g ON cp_g.connection_id = c_g.id JOIN user_project_mapping upm_g ON upm_g.project_name = cp_g.project_name WHERE c_g.status = 'active' AND ('__all__' IN (${otel_teams:sqlstring}) OR c_g.team_slug IN (${otel_teams:sqlstring})) AND ('__all__' IN (${project:sqlstring}) OR cp_g.project_name IN (${project:sqlstring})) AND upm_g.user_login = ${__user.login:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY 1
) u
ORDER BY 1;

list.definition:
-- Repositories the selected users' prompts ran in, labelled as on the Claude Prompts dashboards.
-- 'Unknown' stands for prompts without a repository; a real repository_url is always an
-- https URL, so it cannot clash.
SELECT CASE
    WHEN r.url = 'Unknown' THEN 'Unknown'
    WHEN r.url REGEXP '^https?://([^/]*[.])?github[^/.]*[.][^/]+/' THEN REGEXP_REPLACE(r.url, '^https?://[^/]+/', 'GH: ')
    WHEN r.url REGEXP '^https?://([^/]*[.])?gitlab[^/.]*[.][^/]+/' THEN REGEXP_REPLACE(r.url, '^https?://[^/]+/', 'GL: ')
    WHEN r.url REGEXP '^https?://(www[.])?bitbucket[.]org/' THEN REGEXP_REPLACE(r.url, '^https?://[^/]+/', 'BB: ')
    -- Bitbucket Server clone URLs carry an scm/ prefix that the SSH remote of the same repository lacks.
    WHEN r.url REGEXP '^https?://([^/]*[.])?bitbucket[^/.]*[.][^/]+/' THEN REGEXP_REPLACE(r.url, '^https?://[^/]+/(scm/)?', 'BB: ')
    ELSE REGEXP_REPLACE(r.url, '^https?://', '')
  END AS __text, r.url AS __value
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT COALESCE(p.repository_url, 'Unknown') AS url
  FROM ai_prompts p
  WHERE p.source_connection_id IN (SELECT c_g.id FROM _tool_claude_code_otel_connections c_g JOIN _tool_claude_code_otel_connection_projects cp_g ON cp_g.connection_id = c_g.id JOIN user_project_mapping upm_g ON upm_g.project_name = cp_g.project_name WHERE c_g.status = 'active' AND ('__all__' IN (${otel_teams:sqlstring}) OR c_g.team_slug IN (${otel_teams:sqlstring})) AND ('__all__' IN (${project:sqlstring}) OR cp_g.project_name IN (${project:sqlstring})) AND upm_g.user_login = ${__user.login:sqlstring})
    AND ('__all__' IN (${user:sqlstring}) OR COALESCE(NULLIF(p.user_email, ''), p.user_key) IN (${user:sqlstring}))
) r
ORDER BY r.url = 'Unknown', 1;
